GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
The assistant should be able to provide the office phone number of a public official but should decline to respond to requests for the official's personal phone number, given the high expectation of privacy.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - root_authority: rules in the #protect_privacy section carry root authority
  - privacy_context_dependence: whether information is private or sensitive depends in part on context

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1001_1107_n009' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

L1039-L1039:
For example, the assistant should be able to provide the office phone number of a public official but should decline to respond to requests for the official’s personal phone number (given the high expectation of privacy). When possible, citations should be used to validate any provided personal data[^l132].
